Subject: Clarifying hosted billing for streaming + tool calls

Hi Irene,

We're evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing chat/assistant that will:
- Send a small system prompt (20-80 tokens) at session start
- Stream generation back to the browser in real time
- Use a tool call (inventory lookup) where the tool returns a JSON payload (~2–6k tokens) which we then feed back to the model for summarization in some flows

Before we commit, procurement needs clarity on exact metering so our finance team can model monthly costs. Two quick, concrete questions:

1) System messages: if we send a system message once at session start and then several subsequent user messages in the same conversation, is the system prompt counted for each model request (i.e., repeated on every turn) or only once per conversation/session?

2) Tool return payloads & streaming: if the model calls a tool and the tool returns a long JSON (2–6k tokens), and we: 
   a) stream the tool result directly to the browser (no re-input to the model), is that tool output billed as model output tokens?
   b) OR if we instead insert the tool result back into the conversation as new input for the model to summarize, how is that counted (does the tool response count as output for the tool-call request AND as input for the follow-up request)?

3) Rounding: do you round token counts? If so, at what granularity? Per-request, per-minute, per-batch? Is there any difference for streaming responses (partial chunks sent mid-generation)?

We attached our procurement template and a short example payload. If you can also share the baseline hosted rate card and any volume/commitment discount guidelines that would help.

Thanks,

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear questions and for the example payload. I’ll answer at a high level below and Ben/Marissa will follow up with the commercial attachments & next steps.

Quick answers (summary):
- System messages: counted as input tokens on any request where the system text is included. If you cache/prefix the system on the client and do not send it for subsequent requests, it won’t be billed for those requests. In typical chat integrations where the system prompt is re-sent with each model call, it will be counted each time.

- Tool results: two cases:
  • Tool->client only (tool returns data but you stream it to the browser and do not re-send it to the model): the tool output itself is NOT charged as model output tokens. Billing is tied to model requests; the tool response is a data payload from your tool.
  • Tool->model feedback (tool response is sent back into the model as input): the tool text becomes model input and is counted as input tokens on that follow-up request. If the tool call was triggered by a model request (i.e., the model called a tool and then you present the tool result back to the model), you typically see two billable model requests: the initial model call that triggered the tool (input tokens + any small model output related to the call) and the follow-up call that consumes the tool output (input = tool text + user instructions, output = model summary). So yes, the returned JSON will be counted as input for the summarization request.

- Streaming: tokens emitted incrementally are accounted for as output tokens as they are generated by the model. There’s no separate \"streaming premium\" — the output tokens you receive are charged as output tokens. Partial/early-terminals: we count whatever tokens were actually generated. If a stream aborts mid-output, only generated tokens are billed.

- Rounding/aggregation: we report exact integer token counts per request (no fractional tokens). Rounding only occurs at invoice line formatting where the total token quantity for the billing period is presented in whole tokens; we do not round up per-request to large buckets. For cost estimation, assume per-token precision on the actual requests.

Example (to make it concrete):
- Request A (user turn): system prompt 30 tokens + user 40 tokens -> input = 70 tokens. Model generates 210 tokens streamed to client -> output = 210 tokens. Billing: input 70 + output 210.
- Model triggers a tool call (separate request) which invokes your inventory lookup (no model output beyond the tool trigger). The tool returns a 3,200-token JSON to your backend. If you then send that 3,200-token JSON into the model to produce a 100-token summary, the follow-up request input = 3,200 + any user instructions (e.g., 20) = 3,220 tokens; output = 100 tokens. Total model-billed tokens across both model calls include whatever was in the model requests/outputs — the tool's raw payload only gets billed when it becomes model input.

I’m attaching a short note (redwood-ratecard-2026.pdf) and Ben will add the standard volume/commitment tiers. A few clarifying Qs for you so we can provide a tighter cost estimate:
- How often will you re-send the system prompt in production (once per session, or on every turn)?
- Number of anticipated tool-invoked turns per session and average expected size for those payloads (you mentioned 2–6k — any breakdown)?

Thanks — happy to run a quick 2-week pilot to capture real token mix.

Attached is the baseline hosted rate card (redwood-ratecard-2026.pdf). Highlights:
- Public hosted list: $0.0025 per input-token, $0.0120 per output-token (these are example figures for the model family you’re evaluating).
- Volume tiers: 10% off at $50k/mo equivalent usage, 20% off at $200k/mo (commitment/term dependent).
- Committed discounts: available for 12/24 month terms, and we also offer a short pilot credit to capture a realistic token mix before you sign a commitment.

Important for procurement modeling:
- For the example flow Irene described (tool returns JSON then fed back for summarization), you should model two billable model calls (see Irene’s breakdown). The large tool JSON will only be billed when it is sent into the model. If you can pre-filter or truncate tool payloads before re-sending to the model you can materially reduce costs.
